ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Bits 1 and 0 are transmitted with equal probability. At the receiver, the pdf of the respective received signals for both bits are as shown in the image. If the detection threshold is 1, what is the BER?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the probability density functions of two received signals. The pdf of bit 0 is a triangle, with vertex at x=0 and height approximately 1, and support interval from x=-1 to x=1, so there is no area to the right of x=1. The pdf of bit 1 is another triangle, with support interval from x=0 to x=4, vertex at x=2 and height 0.5; it rises linearly over the interval from x=0 to x=2. Reasoning: The detection threshold is 1; if the received value is greater than 1, decide bit 1, otherwise decide bit 0. When bit 0 is sent, the error region is the area of the bit 0 pdf for x>1, which from the figure is 0. When bit 1 is sent, the error region is the area of the bit 1 pdf for x<1, namely the small triangle below from x=0 to x=1. Since the bit 1 pdf rises linearly from height 0 at x=0 to height 0.5 at x=2, the height at x=1 is 0.25. This error area is (1/2)×1×0.25 = 1/8. The two bits are sent with equal probability, so BER = 0.5×0 + 0.5×(1/8) = 1/16.

raw_record.question_text: Bits 1 and 0 are transmitted with equal probability. At the receiver, the pdf of the respective received signals for both bits are as shown in the image. If the detection threshold is 1, what is the BER?

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted pdfs: bit 0 has zero support beyond x=1, while bit 1 rises linearly from x=0 to the peak at x=2. With threshold 1, the bit-0 error area to the right of 1 is zero. The bit-1 error area is the small triangle under the bit-1 pdf from x=0 to x=1; since the height at x=1 is halfway from 0 to 0.5, it is 0.25, so this area is (1/2)(1)(0.25)=1/8. Average the two conditional errors with equal priors: BER = 0.5(0+1/8)=1/16.

method.method_draft: From the plotted coordinates, write the bit-1 pdf on the rising segment 0≤x≤2 as f1(x)=x/4, and note the bit-0 pdf has support only up to x=1, so ∫_1^∞ f0(x)dx=0. The threshold 1 means a bit-1 is mistaken as bit 0 when x<1, so compute ∫_0^1 x/4 dx=1/8. Combine conditional errors using equal prior probabilities: BER=(1/2)·0+(1/2)·(1/8)=1/16.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The plot shows two triangular probability density functions. The pdf for bit 0 is a triangle supported from x = -1 to x = 1, with peak value 1 at x = 0. The pdf for bit 1 is a triangle supported from x = 0 to x = 4, with peak value 0.5 at x = 2. Reasoning: With detection threshold 1, a received value below 1 is detected as bit 0 and a received value above 1 is detected as bit 1. For bit 0, the pdf has no support beyond x = 1, so P(error | bit 0) = integral from 1 to infinity of f0(x) dx = 0. For bit 1, an error occurs when x < 1. On the rising segment from x = 0 to x = 2, the bit-1 pdf is the line through (0,0) and (2,0.5), so f1(x) = x/4. Thus P(error | bit 1) = integral from 0 to 1 of x/4 dx = [x^2/8]_0^1 = 1/8. Since bits 0 and 1 are equally likely, BER = (1/2)(0) + (1/2)(1/8) = 1/16.
